claims.text: A hook is called by the harness on every matching event, runs with the user's permissions, and can block the action, ask a person, or rewrite what the model reads.
claims.quote: It runs with the user's permissions.

claims.text: Hooks are the agent's kernel, and today we write them like scripts.
claims.quote: Hooks are the agent's kernel, and today we write them like scripts.

claims.text: Hooks should be managed like kernel code: small, reviewed by more than one person, versioned, tested on fixed inputs, signed, installed where the agent cannot write.
claims.quote: So we should manage them like kernel code.

claims.text: A hook can be five lines, so the whole review graph from the intent it serves to every line it calls fits on one page and can be done completely.
claims.quote: A hook can be five lines.

claims.text: The three hooks this session runs are in one 216-line file: re-anchoring in 9 lines, the prompt summary in 14, and the stop check in 26.
claims.quote: The three this session runs are in one 216-line file

value.unit: lines in the shared hooks file

claims.text: The first ten hooks are 4 to 26 lines each; the eleven-line commit hook calls a 37-line scan.
claims.quote: 4 to 26 lines each; the eleven-line commit hook calls a 37-line scan.

claims.text: A hook of hooks: at session start, check every installed hook against a signed list of hashes and refuse to start if one has changed.
claims.quote: A hook at session start that checks every installed hook against a signed list of hashes

claims.text: A security review agent hook reviews a push before it leaves, on the most capable model, with read-only tools and no network.
claims.quote: This is where the most capable model belongs: a security review should be as effective as possible.

claims.text: In the sandbox the leak scan let a GitHub token shape through because its patterns were written for this site's own secrets; the hook was correct and the code below it incomplete.
claims.quote: the scan let a GitHub token shape through because its patterns were written for this site's own secrets

claims.text: Change one pattern in the shared scan and the climb reaches the commit gate for every session that installs it; the graph shows which changes are large whatever the size of the diff.
claims.quote: Change one pattern in the shared scan, and the climb reaches the commit gate for every session that installs it.

claims.text: Claude Code lists five kinds of hook handler: a command, an HTTP call, an MCP tool, a prompt hook and an agent.
claims.quote: Claude Code lists five kinds of handler

claims.text: A maturity model of five levels for how a rule is kept: L0 in the prompt, L1 a model decides, L2 a deterministic script, L3 managed and proven, L4 off the machine.
claims.quote: The levels say how the rule is kept, building on the barrier types of a behaviour policy

claims.text: Three questions for every hook at any level: how much power it has, which legs of the lethal trifecta it touches, and how much sandbox it runs in.
claims.quote: And three questions for every hook, at any level.

claims.text: The less deterministic a hook is, the less it should be able to reach; full internet access for an agent inside a hook is hard to justify.
claims.quote: The less deterministic a hook is, the less it should be able to reach.

claims.text: All ten hooks are L2 or proposed; none is L3, because this session's own hooks live in a folder the agent can write.
claims.quote: All ten hooks in the figure are L2 or proposed.

claims.text: Isolated agent environments such as Chainguard's, where every run produces a signed record, are where a hook's tests should run and an agent hook can be kept from the network.
claims.quote: an environment where every run is isolated and produces a signed record of what ran is exactly where a hook's tests should run

claims.text: A hooks site and feed, the hooks equivalent of a skills manager, where every hook starts from the behaviour policy row it serves and carries its graph, fixtures, version, hash and signature.
claims.quote: So the proposal is a site and a feed to manage the hooks we deploy, the hooks equivalent of a skills manager.

claims.text: Installing and running a hook is free and works offline; paying buys state: the history of decisions, alerts, the footprint against the policy, signed attestations and managed updates.
claims.quote: Installing and running a hook is free, and it works offline

claims.text: The billing principle is the reading meter's on sgit.ai: nobody is forced to pay.
claims.quote: the same principle as the reading meter on sgit.ai: nobody is forced to pay

claims.text: The feed is a hooks.json file and a page per hook; abp.sgit.ai, where the behaviour policy is published, is a natural home.
claims.quote: abp.sgit.ai, where the behaviour policy is published, is a natural home

claims.text: Nothing in the feed or a usage record carries a key, a secret or the content the hook saw, only the decision; the site publishes defensive hooks, not ways around them.
claims.quote: Nothing in the feed or a usage record carries a key, a secret or the content the hook saw, only the decision.

claims.text: Nothing in the brief is built: the site, the feed, the graph per hook and the billing are proposals.
claims.quote: Nothing in the brief is built.

claims.text: The ten hooks are this session's: three in use, five tested on fixed inputs, two proposed, and none is L3.
claims.quote: Three in use, five tested on fixed inputs, two proposed; none is L3.

claims.text: Line counts are non-blank code lines; the three session hooks were counted inside their shared file.
claims.quote: Line counts are non-blank code lines.

claims.text: The maturity model is a proposal whose levels build on the barrier types this site uses; others would draw them differently.
claims.quote: The maturity model is a proposal.

claims.text: The memo was cut short, exported before it finished; the article covers what it said.
claims.quote: It was exported before it finished; this covers what it said.

claims.text: The article is from a voice memo of 14 October 2026 written by the site's writer agent; the handler types are from Anthropic's Claude Code hooks reference read the same day.
claims.quote: the handler types are from Anthropic's Claude Code hooks reference, read the same day
